title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Count each value, group values into frequency buckets, then collect the k most frequent values from the highest buckets.
note: Assume 1 <= k <= the number of distinct input values. The frequency of any value is at most nums.size, so nums.size + 1 buckets cover every possible frequency.
notes: list(nums.size + 1, list) calls the list factory separately for each bucket. The type list[list[int]] is inferred from the values pushed into those buckets.
counter(nums) produces counter[int]. The key/count loop visits distinct numbers in first-appearance order; values with the same frequency enter their bucket in that order.
reverse buckets visits frequencies from highest to lowest without creating a reversed list. extend appends every value from the current bucket in its existing order.
res[:k] allocates a shallow copy of the first k elements. The size check ensures the prefix is in bounds and limits the result to exactly k values.
With the stated k constraint, the loop returns before the final fallback. The final return keeps a list result explicit on every path.
Under the usual constant-cost hashing, equality, and integer-operation assumptions, the bucket algorithm takes expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space. It does not sort the input or mutate it.
